# Decisions, claims and evidence

Candidate distinctions: a **proposal** presents a possible choice; a **decision** is a choice by an identified authority within a scope; a **claim** asserts something; **evidence** is information used to support or challenge a claim. Evidence is a role in an argument, not necessarily a mutually exclusive kind of object.

A decision occurrence is different from its record. A proposal can describe a system; “proposed” does not replace “system” as its kind. A discussion summary can preserve a decision but does not authorize choices it merely recommends.

Accepted, implemented, operating, evaluated and effective are distinct standings. A design can be accepted and unimplemented, implemented and unevaluated, or once effective and now unsuitable. Claim scope includes subject, version, conditions and period. Evidence confidence is separate from degree of requirement achievement and from acceptance.

For this collection, one decision file contains only the decision in its body, with dates, authority, rationale, source discussion, affected documents, incorporation and supersession in frontmatter. This is an authoring choice, not yet a universal operating-model storage mandate.

EOM-01, EOM-06 and EOM-08 remain open in [the ledger](../../../../source-locators.md#source-c43947fdcdae322a). See [identity and change](../identity-and-change.md), [assessment](../../assessment/requirement-and-need-fulfillment.md), and [records](../../information-model/records-and-provenance.md).
